recipes.name: Apple Pie in a Jar Drink
ingredients_raw: 1.5 cups white sugar, or to taste
1 (1 liter) bottle 190 proof grain alcohol (such as Everclear™)

steps.text: Inspect 9 (quart-sized) jars for cracks and rings for rust, discarding any defective ones. Immerse in simmering water until drink mix is ready. Wash new, unused lids and rings in warm soapy water.

Combine apple cider, apple juice, sugar, and cinnamon sticks in a large pot over medium-high heat; bring to a boil, stirring until sugar has dissolved. Off heat, discard cinnamon sticks. Cool mixture to room temperature, about 4 hours; stir in grain alcohol.
Pour drink mix into sterilized canning jars. Wipe rims with a moist paper towel to remove any residue. Top with lids and screw rings on tightly. Store in the refrigerator for up to 6 months.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Pie in a Jar Drink
raw_recipe.description: This adult apple pie drink in a jar recipe is made with apple cider, apple juice, grain alcohol, cinnamon, and sugar — a great fall campfire cocktail.

review.reviewBody: make sure your juice is COLD - below room temp- to avoid evaporating the alchohol

I have had this EXACT recipe for years and always have a steady supply in the fridge once deer hunting season comes around. We ARE deer camp. my tips--- SIMMER for 2-3 hours!!! put as much back in the gallon jugs after its finished. very easy to store in fridge and then just a screw cap on it. BUT make it a week or two ahead of time! then put 3 sticks in each gallon jugs and let it sit in the fridge- every couple days shake them up. this way you wont even taste the everclear- if you make it right you wont even know it has alcohol in it. the longer it sits the less alcohol you wil taste. as i dont like hard alcohol i make it early so i can celebrate a downed deer with my husband and all his friends! OH- and make SURE you have a big funnel-- that two bucks at walmart will prevent you from moping a huge mess up in the kitchen. good luck and enjoy!!

I have requests for this year round. I only add 1 cup of sugar or splenda, and I always place a fresh cinnamon stick in each jar. I boil the lids and rings and actually "can" the apple pie, no refridgeration is necessary and if you can keep it around long enough will last a year or more!

I've made this for years & I add 4 cups of sugar & let it simmer until the cinnamon sticks start to uncurl. Also run it through a strainer to fibers from the cinnamon out. I've see people commenting that all they can taste & smell is the everclear. I always hear that they can't even tell there's any alcohol in it. It keeps in the fridge forever. We've had it last for over a year. If you keep it that long the everclear taste does come out more. If that happens just add some more apple juice

I make this at home - this recipe will make up to 9 quarts - so get 9 cinnamon sticks to boil with and add to the jars when you pour it in - I also add in 1 1/2 cups of light brown sugar - by the time you add in the Everclear, figure it around 25-30 proof - taste even better heated up!

Everyone loves this! My notes - 1) boil w/the stix but remove when cooled. 2) Peel apples and cut at least 9 rings an put them in the canning jars - they're a special treat :) 3) I cover the jars with cheese cloth while filling
Great recipe. Used 1/2 gallon of apple cider and 1 gallon of apple juice. Upped the sugar to 2 cups and added 1 Liter and half of Everclear, kept cinnamon sticks the same.

Love this! We usually make half a recipe since it's such a large amount. We use sugar to taste, but I believe we come close to the amount called for, maybe a little more! Sugar helps mask the flavor of Everclear. This is so yummy and the apple juice with cinnamon sticks smells awesome while cooking! Don't add the Everclear to the juice until the juice is completely cooled down after cooking.

I make this recipe every Fall. I usually do half white and half brown sugar, but I think this year I'm going to try cutting the sweetness back just a bit. I also always add half a cup of vanilla vodka when I add the Everclear. Yummm!!!

I originally tried the crockpot version, however it had way to much cinnamon flavor to it. The one thing that I did change up was that I replaced half of the ever clear with Vanilla Bean Sky Vodka and what a difference it made! It actually made it more dangerous because you really couldn't taste the ever clear because the vodka mellowed it out but it still had the kick! People are sending in requests for Christmas already!

I Love this recipe! This is our favorite 'go-to' drink, we make it all the time. I let the juice simmer for an hour or so, then I'll throw a hand full of red hot candies in the cider while it's simmering for a little extra cinnamon flavor. I like to use 1/2 c white sugar and 3/4 c brown sugar.. I think it makes it taste more like apple pie. If you're using moonshine instead of everclear, I'd add and extra 1/4 c of sugar and make sure you give it time to mellow. The most important thing to know about this recipe is that it needs to Mellow. As hard as it is sometimes.. bottle it up and put it away. Open up a jar in three months and THEN decide what you think of this recipe. OMG, amazing.
I always make a batch but with two gallons of apple juice and one bottle of sparkling apple cider. Everyone prefers it that way. And it never makes it past the holidays.
Love this I also put in some Caramel moonshine an fireball whiskey it's really good
Be careful just to stick with one cinnamon stick in a jar or it tastes like red hots. Good stuff though added captain Morgan spiced rum delicious
I love it so easy to make
Delicious! Could definitely cut the sugar down by about 1/3 if you would like.

Great recipe. This drink has been a favorite of mine but I always got it from friends. This recipe was great and was even better after a few months in the fridge. We noticed the flavors got better the longer it sat. I will be making this recipe again.

Not a everclear fan so instead I put in Capt. Morgans spiced rum 100 proof. Gives it a bit more apple pie spice taste . I give it away for Christmas but make sure I have plenty of my own as this is a great drink on chilly nites by the firepit.
Looks delish. Would this be a good shot recipe? How many shots would this recipe make if so please??

I made this and it was delicious. I will say I did not go completely by the directions. I doubled the apple juice, apple cider and cinnamon sticks. I simmered it for 12 hours. Then the store only had 750 ml of Everclear bottles, so I bought three and used all of them. I completely forgot the sugar which was fine because it was sweet enough. We could barely taste the alcohol, the only way we knew it was there was the warmth in are throats and chest. Completely underestimated how much alcohol was in there and my friends party was a hit because I brought these along.
